pattern: Answers that state the conclusion first and then give reasoning were rated clearer than long unstructured explanations.
Candidates who backed every claim with a specific project or internship example scored higher than those who only gave definitions.
Generic statements about learning and growth without a concrete story were repeatedly marked down.
Interviewers noted candidates who could not state the time and space complexity of their own code.
Analysts were rated higher when they connected a metric to a business decision rather than only describing the technique.
Panels repeatedly tested DBMS, OOP and one programming language in depth; weak basics were penalised more than lack of advanced topics.
Feedback often mentioned willingness to relocate, learn and adapt as an important soft-signal.
Candidates who explained their approach before writing code were rated better than those who started typing immediately.
Questions frequently dug into the candidate's own project; vague answers about personal contribution were marked down.
Speed and accuracy in basic aptitude was noted; showing steps clearly helped partial credit.
Candidates who confused DELETE, TRUNCATE and DROP or the join types lost marks on database rounds.
Overloading versus overriding and HashMap internals appeared in feedback as common gaps.
Clear and calm communication under pressure was repeatedly highlighted in positive feedback.
Panels liked basic awareness of cloud, REST and Agile; buzzword use without explanation was marked down.
Behavioural answers with a clear own-action and result were rated higher than answers describing only the team.
Candidates were expected to move from a brute-force solution to an optimised one and justify the trade-off aloud.
Answers without measurable results or the candidate's own actions (using I instead of we) were scored low.
Clarifying requirements and stating trade-offs before drawing components was rated better than jumping into a design.
Feedback highlighted the need for crisp basics in SQL, OOP and one language; rambling answers were penalised.
Candidates who knew the company's services and could link them to their interests were rated higher in HR rounds.
